# Ropedia Raises $30 Million to Scale Data Infrastructure for Physical AI
![](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/03073b76e13f90fdffadf3010f2aef4236930f550cdf1fe9afbcdf5f5559c21f/lightyear_networkapi/resizefit_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fbusiness-wire.com%2F95692f30c10f5273fbd37375aa8cf569)

Business Wire

July 23, 20265 min read

_Funds were raised in two pre-A rounds and will back global expansion of the company's real-world interaction data platform for robotics and embodied AI systems_

**SINGAPORE, July 23, 2026**--( [BUSINESS WIRE](https://www.businesswire.com/))-- [Ropedia](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fropedia.com%2F&esheet=54575292&newsitemid=20260723509119&lan=en-US&anchor=Ropedia&index=1&md5=1cdd41706467cac948b9eb9a3f1abdc5), a Singapore-based startup building data infrastructure for physical AI, today announced it has raised US$30 million dollars in pre-A funding from venture investors with deep experience in AI, enterprise technology and infrastructure across Southeast Asia. Funding will scale Ropedia's collection of real-world, multimodal interaction data and expand delivery to technology companies developing robots and embodied AI systems.

"A robot can't play baseball by watching a video any more than you could learn to ride a bike by reading about it. The robot must understand what it's like to grip a bat and know the timing it takes to hit a ball. Real-world human experience, captured at the same scale, will train physical AI.

From real-world sensing to model-ready intelligence, physical AI requires an end-to-end data pipeline. [**HOMIE**](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fropedia.com%2Fblog%2F20251216_introducing_ropedia&esheet=54575292&newsitemid=20260723509119&lan=en-US&anchor=HOMIE&index=2&md5=e204895f02ce2704715ba5e946e1c437), Ropedia's wearable, head-mounted device, captures first-person video, audio, depth, hand tracking, gaze, body motion and camera pose simultaneously, with each stream timestamped.

The company operates a "closed-loop pipeline" that integrates multimodal synchronization and rigorous quality assurance into dataset generation and model-aligned fine-tuning. Unlike teleoperation-based systems, which are constrained by expensive robot fleets, the platform scales simply by adding wearable capture devices.

Story Continues

This infrastructure powers [**Xperience-10M**](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fhuggingface.co%2Fdatasets%2Fropedia-ai%2Fxperience-10m&esheet=54575292&newsitemid=20260723509119&lan=en-US&anchor=Xperience-10M&index=3&md5=100a311e5de1169b16432707e788f6a9), one of the largest human-experience datasets in the industry: 10 million interaction episodes and more than 10,000 hours of multimodal recordings, spanning billions of synchronized video, depth, motion-capture and inertial-sensor frames.

The latest round, announced today, raised US$22 million and follows an earlier US$8 million round announced on social media on March 16, for a total of US$30 million.

One of its angel investors, a research scientist from Amazon, said, "I backed the Ropedia team early because they had a rare combination of deep technical expertise, speed of execution and a clear vision for where physical AI was heading. Since then, they have built a compelling data infrastructure platform serving leading robotics and foundation-model companies globally.

Robotics and physical AI lab customers get more data, delivered faster, across a wider range of environments and tasks.

Ropedia builds data infrastructure for physical AI.

news.title: Ropedia raises $22M to scale human-centric data collection for embodied AI
news.snippet:
Ropedia raises $22M to scale human-centric data collection for embodied AI - SiliconANGLE [Skip to content](https://siliconangle.com/2026/07/23/ropedia-raises-22m-scale-human-centric-data-collection-embodied-ai/#sa-page-content)

### Ropedia raises $22M to scale human-centric data collection for embodied AI
![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/b0aab96da155e611d7deba4d7b1b7632c27bf59f8448f335a1ab2e86a206dabc?s=96&r=pg)

by [Kyt Dotson](https://siliconangle.com/author/kitdotson/)

Singapore-based robotics data infrastructure firm [Ropedia Pte. Ltd.](https://ropedia.com/) today announced it raised $22 million in Pre-Series A funding to scale up its collection of real-world, multimodal interaction data to fuel artificial intelligence robotics models developed by technology companies.

[Physical AI](https://siliconangle.com/2025/12/28/beyond-automation-physical-ai-ushers-new-era-smart-machines/) and embodied AI development is increasingly burdened by a lack of real-world data at a diversity and scale that robot-specific teleoperation struggles to produce. Developers in this field need models that can generalize across robots, objects and environments to scale products. Ropedia’s industry proposition is to gather human experience directly via video and convert it into model-ready multimodal datasets.

Although images and text exist in abundance, and there are many videos online, much of it cannot be readily curated or transformed into robotic trajectories that represent human-like activity. When a robot interacts with the real world, it needs synchronized, annotated, and curated information about movements, geometry and the consequences of those actions. Pictures of objects don’t work for this and unless video is well structured, it’s harder to concentrate into a clean dataset.

“There’s not yet going to be a massive deployment of robots,” founder and Chief Executive Zhaoxi Chen told SiliconANGLE in an interview. “We need to unlock the ChatGPT moment for robotics first.”

![](https://siliconangle.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2026/07/image-3-800x449.png)

### Revolutionizing future robotics with curated data
The company’s data-centric foundation is already paying off. Chen noted that the Allen Institute for AI, a preeminent AI research company developing AI models, [recently released MolmoMotion](https://allenai.org/blog/molmo-motion), a 3D motion forecasting model that can anticipate how objects will move within a scene. He explained that Ropedia supplied more than half of the data sources used to train the model.

Chen said the new funding will help Ropedia put its second-generation HOMIE hardware into large-scale production, with an eventual target of as many as 10,000 devices. The company also intends to hire across hardware, software, AI infrastructure and business development, including talent focused on efficiency and performance for its annotation models.

At its core, Ropedia provides clean data for robotics. According to Chen, it’s an emerging discipline and it’s fundamental to the foundation that will allow embodied AI and smart robotics to scale up.

“Data is also a form of science,” Chen said. “It’s not only about collecting or accumulating the data. It’s more like how you organize and understand the flow between different domains.”

news.title: Here’s A $32 Million Bet That Robots Don’t Need A Billion Dollars Of Real-World Data

# Here’s A $32 Million Bet That Robots Don’t Need A Billion Dollars Of Real-World Data
## Summary
Figure AI launched Index, a billion-dollar initiative to gather real-world data for robot training, collecting 16 million videos globally. However, Antioch, a startup led by Harry Mellsop, secured $32 million to champion simulated data as a more affordable and efficient alternative. Antioch's platform creates high-fidelity simulations, accelerating physical AI development by allowing cloud-scale testing without constant hardware validation.

VCG via Getty Images

It’s a [billion-dollar bet](https://www.forbes.com/sites/johnkoetsier/2026/08/26/figure-launches-gig-platform-to-get-humans-to-do-work-to-train-robots-will-spend-1-billion/) on real-world data for robot AI training, and it’s also a distributed data engine that has already collected more than 16 million videos from 108 countries, paid out $15 million to the people who shot them, and carries a commitment of over $1 billion in data and compute over the next 12 months.

“If you’re a company like Figure, and you have the resources to go and do something like that, that’s fantastic,” Mellsop told me in an interview last week.

Mellsop is the co-founder of Antioch, a New York-based robot training data startup that today announced a $32 million Series A led by Greylock, with participation from A*, Category Ventures, Box Group and Icehouse Ventures. the core premise: simulated data is good enough to train tomorrow’s humanoid robots.

Instead, it charges customers a recurring fee that Webb said is less than the cost of hiring warehouse workers directly. Customers know the machines are remote workers in robotic bodies, Webb said.

There's a bigger prize buried in this arrangement. news.title: General Intuition Raises $220M to Scale World Models for Physical AI
news.snippet:
# General Intuition Raises $220M to Scale World Models for Physical AI
September 30, 2026

![General Intuition Raises $220M to Scale World Models for Physical AI](https://ihfyvnmcmnvwrtmuemaa.supabase.co/storage/v1/render/image/public/blog-images/1790779877687-blue-and-beige-modern-europe-travel-presentation-2026-09-30t.png?width=1600&quality=88&height=900&resize=contain)

## Highlights
- General Intuition raised $220 million at a $6.2 billion valuation.
- Its MIRA world model was trained on 10,000 hours of Rocket League data and runs in real time at 20 frames per second.

## General Intuition Adds $220M to Its World-Model Push
General Intuition has raised an additional **$220 million** at a **$6.2 billion valuation**, giving the world-model startup more capital to develop AI systems designed to perceive environments, predict outcomes and take actions.

The round includes **Valor Equity Partners, Atreides, Seven Seven Six, Point72, Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst**.

The financing comes as General Intuition begins making its models available to external partners, expanding beyond its earlier research and limited collaborations in gaming, simulation and robotics.

The company was spun out of gaming platform Medal, which provides access to a large source of gameplay footage. General Intuition uses action-labeled video from these environments as training data for models intended to learn how actions affect the world.

## Using Gameplay as Training Data for AI Agents
That creates a large supply of data linking **what an agent sees with what action it takes**.

General Intuition says its models are trained on action-labeled video datasets collected across many environments.

## MIRA Demonstrates the World-Model Approach
General Intuition says MIRA was trained on **10,000 hours of data collected using publicly available bots** and learned the dynamics of a four-player Rocket League environment.

## Medal Provides a Large Data Pipeline
General Intuition uses this ecosystem as a source of video showing people interacting with virtual environments.

The company says players upload billions of gameplay clips each year, creating a large pool of action-linked visual data.

That gives General Intuition a different training-data strategy from companies primarily collecting demonstrations from physical robots.

Instead of relying entirely on real-world robotic interactions, the company can first expose its models to large numbers of virtual environments and actions.

The approach also allows researchers to experiment with environments that would be expensive or dangerous to reproduce physically.

## Funding Accelerates the World-Model Platform
The new $220 million financing gives General Intuition additional resources to scale its research infrastructure, develop its models and expand access to partners.

With additional capital and a growing training-data pipeline through Medal, General Intuition is now moving from demonstrating world-model capabilities toward building an external platform for AI systems that need to perceive environments, predict outcomes and act within them.
